ghs.en: Nanaka: "Yahooo, Taicchan!"
Taichi: "Oh my?"
The cycling woman of mystery.
Taichi: "The cycling woman of mystery."

rows.jp: 思ったまま口にしてしまった。
rows.en: I’d gone and said exactly what I was thinking.

ghs.en: Dammit, thoughts passed through the mouth!
ghs.assessment: The source says he accidentally spoke exactly what he was thinking. “Thoughts passed through the mouth” is an impersonal calque that does not express his action.
ghs.remedy: Use “I accidentally said exactly what I was thinking.”

highlights.text: Dammit, thoughts passed through the mouth!

rows.jp: 「思ったまま口にしないように」
rows.en: “Try not to say every thought out loud.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "I wish you wouldn't pass thoughts through the mouth."
ghs.assessment: Nanaka tells him not to voice every thought. Repeating “pass thoughts through the mouth” preserves the same non-English construction.
ghs.remedy: Use “Try not to say everything that crosses your mind.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "I wish you wouldn't pass thoughts through the mouth."

ghs.en: Discovered.
ghs.assessment: ばれていた is a terse resultant passive, and Discovered can elliptically mean found out. The English remains ambiguous and unnatural rather than semantically unrelated.
ghs.remedy: Use They had found me out or equivalent.

highlights.text: Discovered.

rows.jp: 「あやしいんだよなー、この女。素性は不明だし。見たこと無い制服だし」
rows.en: “There’s something fishy about this woman. I don’t know the first thing about her, and I’ve never seen that uniform before.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Suspicious, ain't she, this female. Origins and background unknown. Uniform that I have never seen."
ghs.assessment: The Japanese itself is clipped and clinically suspicious. Preserve that fragmentation; only forms such as this female are unnaturally dehumanizing in English.
ghs.remedy: Keep the clipped suspicion in natural English.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Suspicious, ain't she, this female. Origins and background unknown. Uniform that I have never seen."

rows.jp: 「……開き直って思考を言葉に仮託(かたく)しないように」
rows.en: “...And don’t double down by turning your thoughts into a running commentary.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...I wish you wouldn't turn defiant and use thoughts as pretext for words."
ghs.assessment: She tells him not to get defiant and pass his thoughts off as spoken words. “Use thoughts as pretext for words” reverses the representational relation.
ghs.remedy: Use “And don’t get defiant and start passing your thoughts off as dialogue.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "...I wish you wouldn't turn defiant and use thoughts as pretext for words."

rows.jp: 「七香って名前だって本当なのかどうか」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Nanaka she says her name is, but is that the truth?"
ghs.assessment: The source questions whether Nanaka is even her real name. “Nanaka she says her name is” uses malformed inversion.
ghs.remedy: Use “For all I know, even the name Nanaka may be fake.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Nanaka she says her name is, but is that the truth?"

rows.jp: 「……うっさいわね。細かいことグダグダ言うんじゃないわよ」
rows.en: “...God, you’re annoying. Quit nitpicking every little thing.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...shaddap you. Don't just keep fussing tediously on the details."
ghs.assessment: Shaddap is deliberate coarse eye dialect matching Nanaka's voice. The confirmed defect is the awkward phrase fussing tediously on the details.
ghs.remedy: Keep the coarse interruption and repair the following idiom.

highlights.text: Nanaka: "...shaddap you. Don't just keep fussing tediously on the details."

ghs.en: Taichi: "What school do you go to?"
Nanaka: "Shi-kuh-ret."
Taichi: "Ah, right."

rows.jp: 無視してさっさと歩き出す。
rows.en: I ignored her and walked on.

ghs.en: I ignore her and quickly walk on.
Nanaka: "Oh, hard-boild'y～!"

rows.jp: 「歩きながらでも話せるだろうに」

ghs.en: Taichi: "We can talk even while walking you know."
Nanaka: "Yah whatev'."
Taichi: "So, got business?"

rows.jp: 「もちろん用事があるわけさ」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "'Course I'm here on business!"

rows.en: She jabbed a finger at me.

ghs.en: She points close at me.
ghs.assessment: The source says she points sharply or decisively. “Points close at me” changes manner into physical proximity.
ghs.remedy: Use “She pointed sharply at me.”

highlights.text: She points close at me.

rows.jp: 「とっととアンテナ組み立てる！」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Put that antenna together right quick!"
Taichi: "Huh?"

rows.jp: 「アンテナって、見里先輩のやってるやつ？」

ghs.en: Taichi: "The antenna, that thing Misato-senpai's doing you mean?"
Nanaka: "Yep, that."

rows.jp: 「このままじゃちょっと間に合わないよ」
rows.en: “At this rate, it won’t be ready in time.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "At this rate you might not make it in time!"
Taichi: "To what?"
Nanaka: "Time limit."
Taichi: "Of what?"
Nanaka: "Ohhh really, youuu!"
Taichi: "Wh-, what's with that!"

rows.jp: いきなり怒りだしたぞ。
rows.en: She’d blown up at me out of nowhere.

ghs.en: She flew off the handle all of a sudden.

rows.jp: 「一回一回が、大事な人生でしょうが！　調子こいてるといつまでもいつまでも無駄にしちゃって、そのうち存在自体が固定行動に固着しちゃうんだからね！」
rows.en: “Every single time, it’s a whole, precious life! Keep screwing around and wasting them over and over, and before long your very existence will get stuck repeating the same fixed pattern!”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Once, just once, live like your life's precious! But you get caught in the moment and always but always waste it all, and before you know it your very existence is stuck into fixed behaviors!"
ghs.assessment: The source says every single occasion in life is precious, then warns repeated waste hardens existence into fixed behavior. “Once, just once, live” changes the distributive claim into a one-time command.
ghs.remedy: Use “Every single moment matters in a life! If you keep wasting them, your whole existence will eventually harden into fixed behavior!”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Once, just once, live like your life's precious! But you get caught in the moment and always but always waste it all, and before you know it your very existence is stuck into fixed behaviors!"

rows.jp: 「可能性ってのはそーいう性質があるんだから！　ウィン○ウズだって一時キャッシュのせいでリセットしたつもりでもエラーを繰り返すことがあるでしょーに！　ことに今は―――」
rows.en: “Possibilities work like that! Even Win○ows can keep repeating the same error after you thought you reset it, all because of a temporary cache! Especially right now—”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Because possibilities have that as their nature! It's like when you go to reset Wi***ws because of problems in the temporary cache and then you find that it has the same error over again! Especially now it's---"
ghs.assessment: GHS still links the reset to temporary-cache trouble followed by recurrence of the same error. The residual-cache causality is less exact, not erased.
ghs.remedy: State the cache residue and repeated error relation more precisely.

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Because possibilities have that as their nature! It's like when you go to reset Wi***ws because of problems in the temporary cache and then you find that it has the same error over again! Especially now it's---"

rows.jp: ハッとして、口をつぐむ。
rows.en: She stopped short and clammed up.

ghs.en: Startled, she shuts her mouth.
Taichi: "...neurotic are ya, little bastard?"

rows.jp: 「こんなキューティーつかまえて貴様なんて言うなあ！」
rows.en: “Don’t you call a cutie like me an asshole!”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ya don't call this kyute catch a 'bastard' you DON'T!"
ghs.assessment: The source says not to call a cutie like her 貴様. “This kyute catch” is ungrammatical and turns つかまえて into literal catching.
ghs.remedy: Use “Don’t call a cutie like me ‘you bastard’!”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Ya don't call this kyute catch a 'bastard' you DON'T!"

ghs.en: Smaaack!
Taichi: "Uh'owfuu!"
That was one in the face.

rows.jp: 高速でスピンしつつ斜めに跳ね上がり、水平になった状態で地面に叩きつけられた。
rows.en: I spun into the air at high speed, rising at an angle before leveling out horizontally and slamming into the ground.

ghs.en: While spinning at highway speeds I am sprung diagonally, and as my status became horizontal I smacked into the ground.
ghs.assessment: The source says he spins at high speed, springs diagonally upward, becomes horizontal, and slams into the ground. “Highway speeds” invents a road-specific measure, and “as my status became horizontal” is malformed.
ghs.remedy: Use “Spinning at high speed, I flew diagonally upward, leveled out horizontally, and slammed into the ground.”

highlights.text: While spinning at highway speeds I am sprung diagonally, and as my status became horizontal I smacked into the ground.

rows.jp: この娘、コミック力場を発生させることができるとは。
rows.en: So this girl could generate a comic force field.

rows.jp: 太一科学。スカラー電磁学やエーテル宇宙論、昇騰機関などと並ぶ超科学理論のひとつ。あらゆる物理現象を加速すると同時に緩和する。
rows.en: Taichi Science. One of the great theories of superscience, alongside scalar electromagnetism, ether cosmology, and the Ascension Engine. It simultaneously accelerates and mitigates every physical phenomenon.

rows.jp: 結果、通常物理では考えられないコミック本めいた効果を発生させる。統計的に勝ち気幼なじみ的パーソナリティに多く付随し、そのキャラ性を維持するために作用する。
rows.en: The result: comic-book effects impossible under ordinary physics. Statistically, it most often manifests in the strong-willed childhood-friend personality type, where it acts to preserve the character’s defining traits.
“What power... You could conquer the world...”

ghs.en: Taichi: "What power... enough to take over the world..."

rows.jp: 「女の子にそんな皮肉言わないの！」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Don't say sarcastic stuff like that to a girl!"
She graciously helped me to my feet.
Taichi: "Th-, that hueeerts..."

rows.jp: 「天下狙えるってのは、単に腕力とかでなくキャラ的にね」
rows.en: “I meant you could conquer the world on character appeal, not brute force.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "When I said you could take over the world, I didn't mean mere brawn, I meant by characterization!"
Nanaka: "?"

rows.jp: 「キミの科学力のおかげで、あれだけの打撃を受けても生きていられるのだよ」
rows.en: “It’s your scientific powers that let me survive a hit like that.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because of your scientific powers, even getting struck that hard means I can still live!"
Nanaka: "I don't really get it..."

rows.jp: 「でももうちょっとはじけても良かった。スピンしたまま大気圏とか」
rows.en: “But you could’ve launched me a little farther. Sent me spinning right out of the atmosphere, maybe.”

rows.jp: 「まあ普通から外れるためにただ極端に走るだけっていうのも貧困のあらわれだと思うから、メリハリだと思うんだけどさ」
rows.en: “Then again, going to extremes just to be different is its own kind of creative bankruptcy. It’s all in the contrast.”

rows.jp: 「要するに王道に対して常に皮相的な立場を保つって行為は自己顕示欲に支配された瞬間に堕するってことだよね」
rows.en: “Basically, rejecting the mainstream for shallow reasons goes to hell the moment it becomes an ego trip.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "The point is that acting in constant preservation of superficial positions is the easy way, and it's destined to degenerate into moments dominated by conspicuous exhibitionism."

rows.jp: 「おまいはあたしと会話する気があるのか？」
rows.en: “Are ya even trying to have a conversation with me?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Do ya even wanna have a conversation with me?"
Taichi: "...apologies."

rows.jp: 自分でも意味わかってないです。
rows.en: I had no idea what I was talking about either.

ghs.en: I have no idea what that meant myself.
Nanaka: "There are no ways for you, really."
ghs.assessment: The source calls him a hopeless or troublesome guy. “There are no ways for you” is not an English characterization.
ghs.remedy: Use “You’re hopeless.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "There are no ways for you, really."

rows.jp: 呆れ半分、ため息を落とす。
rows.en: She let out a half-exasperated sigh.

ghs.en: Half-disgusted, she lets a sigh fall.
ghs.assessment: 呆れ describes exasperation or disbelief here, not disgust. The English gives her a harsher emotion.
ghs.remedy: Use “Half exasperated, she let out a sigh.”

highlights.text: Half-disgusted, she lets a sigh fall.

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ah, blood's on your cheeky."
ghs.assessment: The source points out blood on his cheek. “Cheeky” is an adjective or playful noun, not the anatomical noun required.
ghs.remedy: Use “Ah, there’s blood on your cheek.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "Ah, blood's on your cheeky."

rows.jp: 「え？　ちょっとだけ力場からはみ出ちゃったのかな？」
rows.en: “Huh? Maybe my cheek slipped a little outside the force field?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Eh? Could this mean that it was a bit out of the boundary of the force field?"
Nanaka: "Still talking 'bout force fields and that stuff!"
Taichi: "I'm alright with my own blood."
Nanaka: "...eh?"

rows.jp: 「いや、血が苦手なものでして」

ghs.en: Taichi: "No, it's just that blood is my weakness, 's all."

rows.jp: その時、七香の顔に去来した表情を、俺はうまく表現できない。
rows.en: I could not put into words the expression that crossed Nanaka’s face then.

ghs.en: I can't describe well those recurring expression that were on Nanaka's face at that moment.
ghs.assessment: The source refers to one hard-to-describe expression passing across Nanaka’s face. “Those recurring expression” has number disagreement and makes it multiple recurring expressions.
ghs.remedy: Use “I can’t adequately describe the expression that crossed Nanaka’s face then.”

highlights.text: I can't describe well those recurring expression that were on Nanaka's face at that moment.

rows.jp: 泣きそうでもあったし、笑っているようでもあった。
rows.en: She looked close to tears, yet almost as though she were smiling.

ghs.en: There was something of the crying, there was something of the laughing.
ghs.assessment: The source says she looked on the verge of tears and also as though she were smiling. “Something of the crying/laughing” is ungrammatical and turns expressions into activities.
ghs.remedy: Use “She looked ready to cry, yet also as though she were smiling.”

highlights.text: There was something of the crying, there was something of the laughing.

rows.jp: とはいえ、単純な泣き笑いとも取れない、根深い葛藤が混入していた。
rows.en: But it was no simple tearful smile. Something deep and conflicted lay beneath it.

ghs.en: That said, I can't take this as simply laughing while crying, as there's a deeply ingrained discord mixed in.
Nanaka: "...Taichi."

rows.jp: 掠れるような声が、唇から流れて。
rows.en: The word left her lips in a hoarse whisper.

ghs.en: A voice that feels roughened flows from her lips.
ghs.assessment: English can metaphorically describe a voice as feeling rough. Feels roughened is awkward, but still conveys 掠れる.
ghs.remedy: Use her voice sounded rough or hoarse.

highlights.text: A voice that feels roughened flows from her lips.

ghs.en: Her face came closer,
together with her damp eyes.

rows.jp: 人間の意識活動というものはたいしたもので。
rows.en: The human mind is a remarkable thing.

ghs.en: This thing known as the conscious activity of the human being is really amazing.

rows.jp: 普通の漫画主人公なら、
rows.en: If I were your average manga protagonist—

ghs.en: But if I were your ordinary manga protagonist,

rows.jp: などと起こる出来事さえ予測できず、戸惑うのがせいぜいなのに。
rows.en: —I wouldn’t even see what was coming. The best I could do would be to stand there bewildered.

ghs.en: I would be exclusively bewildered, unable to predict anything of what was about to happen at all.

rows.jp: 現実人間であるところの俺の脳は『ＫＩＳＳされる！？』というシチュ的にそれしかありえない結末を容易に予測してのけて。
rows.en: Being a real human being, however, my brain had no trouble predicting the only possible outcome of a setup like this: I was about to be KISSED?!

ghs.en: Whereas this brain I have as a real human yet easily pulls off the prediction that we are in a 'chewation-like Event that has the name "I'LL BE KISSED?!" with all other conclusions impossible.
ghs.assessment: The source says his real-human brain easily predicts the only situationally plausible conclusion: he is about to be kissed. The English is syntactically incoherent and invents “chewation-like Event.”
ghs.remedy: Use “My real-human brain easily predicted the only ending the situation allowed: ‘I’m about to be KISSED!?’”

highlights.text: Whereas this brain I have as a real human yet easily pulls off the prediction that we are in a 'chewation-like Event that has the name "I'LL BE KISSED?!" with all other conclusions impossible.

rows.jp: 七香の顔が五センチに迫った時にはもう、キス後に『いかにそれっぽく振る舞うか』といった体面処理について検討していたりするわけだが。
rows.en: By the time Nanaka’s face was two inches from mine, I was already working out the finer points of how to look the part afterward.

ghs.en: At the moment Nanaka's face is but five centimeters away, I am yet already in the process of elaborating post-kiss face-saving responses such as "what sort of behavior is that?!"
ghs.assessment: Before the kiss he is already considering how to act convincingly afterward. The quoted “what sort of behavior is that?!” instead sounds like a rebuke and does not translate いかにそれっぽく振る舞うか.
ghs.remedy: Use “By the time her face was five centimeters away, I was already considering how to look suitably convincing after the kiss.”

highlights.text: At the moment Nanaka's face is but five centimeters away, I am yet already in the process of elaborating post-kiss face-saving responses such as "what sort of behavior is that?!"

rows.jp: ……実際こっちのがリアルなのだが、世の物語にほとんど採用されていない理由は、リアルすぎて物語性とうまく親和しないんだということが素人の俺にもありありとわかった。
rows.en: That was far closer to how people actually thought. And even an amateur like me could see why stories almost never did it: reality this real simply did not mesh with narrative.

ghs.en: ...but while this of mine is realistic, the reason that in the tales of the world it is almost never employed is that stories with an overly realistic nature do not inspire much affinity, and that is something vividly understood even by an amateur such as I.
ghs.assessment: The source concludes that this mental process is realistic but too realistic to mesh with narrativity, which explains its absence from stories. The English says realistic stories fail to ‘inspire affinity’ and tangles the causal relation.
ghs.remedy: Use “This is more realistic, but even I could see that it is too real to mesh with storytelling, which is why stories almost never use it.”

highlights.text: ...but while this of mine is realistic, the reason that in the tales of the world it is almost never employed is that stories with an overly realistic nature do not inspire much affinity, and that is something vividly understood even by an amateur such as I.

rows.jp: リアリティごっこなんだよな、結局。
rows.en: In the end, “realism” in fiction was just another game of pretend.

ghs.en: In the end, it's just a game of pretend-reality.

rows.jp: と内心うんうん頷いてたりして。
rows.en: I was nodding sagely to myself by then.

ghs.en: And those are the innermost thoughts to which I am nodding a yes, yes of agreement.
ghs.assessment: The source says he is inwardly nodding along with his own conclusion. “Thoughts to which I am nodding a yes, yes of agreement” is a heavily calqued construction.
ghs.remedy: Use “I nodded sagely to myself.”

highlights.text: And those are the innermost thoughts to which I am nodding a yes, yes of agreement.

rows.en: More to the point: was this KISS happening or what?

ghs.en: And if I may ask, where's that kiss?
Schloop.
Taichi: "..."

rows.jp: 色気も味気もないＫＩＳＳだった。
rows.en: It was a KISS without a trace of romance—or flavor.

ghs.en: A bland kiss with no sex appeal.

rows.jp: 舌を頬に貼りつけて舐めあげる行為を、ＫＩＳＳと称すればのことだが。
rows.en: If you could call planting your tongue on someone’s cheek and dragging it upward a KISS.

ghs.en: But for the act of putting a tongue on a cheek and licking up to even take the name of K-I-S-S...
ghs.assessment: The source conditionally says this was a kiss only if pressing a tongue to a cheek and licking upward can be called one. The English is a fragment that never completes that condition.
ghs.remedy: Use “That is, if pressing your tongue to someone’s cheek and licking upward can be called a KISS.”

highlights.text: But for the act of putting a tongue on a cheek and licking up to even take the name of K-I-S-S...

rows.jp: 「ツバでもつけておけば治るでしょ」

ghs.en: Nanaka: "I've put some saliva on it, and it'll get well now!"
Taichi: "BWAAAAAAH!!!"

rows.jp: 拳で側頭部を打つ、打つ、打つ！！
rows.en: I punched myself in the temple. Once, twice, three times!!

ghs.en: Fist to the side of the head and strike, strike, strike!!!
ghs.assessment: The source explicitly says the narrator strikes his own temple with his fist again and again. The English drops the subject and possessive, reading like an instruction.
ghs.remedy: Use “I struck myself in the temple with my fist again and again!”

highlights.text: Fist to the side of the head and strike, strike, strike!!!

rows.jp: 「知った風な思索の結末が早とちりか！　こいつめ、こいつめ！　この恥さらしが！」
rows.en: “So all that know-it-all philosophizing ended with me jumping the gun! You idiot! You idiot! You goddamn disgrace!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Jumping to the wrong conclusions with those pretend-knowing thoughts! Damn you, damn you! You disgraceful...!"
Nanaka: "But, yourself, to yourself?!"
ghs.assessment: Nanaka is shocked that he is hitting himself. “But, yourself, to yourself” does not form that reflexive action coherently.
ghs.remedy: Use “Y-you’re hitting yourself!?”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "But, yourself, to yourself?!"

rows.jp: 「なにがリアリティか！　なにが親和か！　頭良いつもりか俺様野郎が！　人以下であることを国際的に証明されている分際で！」
rows.en: “‘Reality,’ my ass! ‘Narrative compatibility,’ my ass! You think you’re so smart, Mr. King Shit? You’re internationally certified as subhuman!”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Reality, are you kidding me! Affinity, are you kidding me! The Greatness that is I thinks he's so smart, the worthless son of a bitch! Your social standing is that of someone who has been internationally proven to be subhuman!"
ghs.assessment: The source is self-directed abuse: he mocks his own pretensions and internationally demonstrated subhuman score. “The Greatness that is I thinks” shifts between first and third person, while “social standing” is added.
ghs.remedy: Use a coherent first-person self-rebuke preserving the reality, affinity, pseudo-intellectual, and test-score insults.

highlights.text: Taichi: "Reality, are you kidding me! Affinity, are you kidding me! The Greatness that is I thinks he's so smart, the worthless son of a bitch! Your social standing is that of someone who has been internationally proven to be subhuman!"

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ca-, calm down..."
Taichi: "I want to die."
Nanaka: "Come now, come now!"

rows.jp: 「いわゆるひとつの自分がゴミであることを自覚していなければならないのです」
rows.en: “I must retain what you might call a certain awareness that I am garbage.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "This one has been making too many wrong mistakes and must therefore awaken to the reality of being garbage."
ghs.assessment: The source says one must recognize that the so-called self is garbage. The English invents a history of “too many wrong mistakes” as the reason.
ghs.remedy: Use “One must recognize that this thing called the self is garbage.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "This one has been making too many wrong mistakes and must therefore awaken to the reality of being garbage."

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...eh?"
Taichi: "Toxic garbage."

rows.jp: 「群青には無識者もたくさんいるから」

ghs.en: Taichi: "Because, there's many people who aren't really aware in Gunjou."
ghs.assessment: The plural existential subject requires “there are,” not “there’s.”
ghs.remedy: Use “There are many unaware people in Gunjou.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Because, there's many people who aren't really aware in Gunjou."

rows.jp: 「俺はいつもこわかったんだ。傷つけてしまわないかって」
rows.en: “I’ve always been scared I might hurt one of them.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I'm always living with fear. I don't want to hurt."
ghs.assessment: The source says he has always feared that he might hurt them. “I don’t want to hurt” omits the object and changes fear of a possible act into a present preference.
ghs.remedy: Use “I’ve always been afraid that I might hurt them.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I'm always living with fear. I don't want to hurt."

rows.jp: 「危険があっても回避できないのが、無識ってことだからね」
rows.en: “Danger-blind means they can’t avoid a threat even when it’s right in front of them.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "Even if there's danger it can't be avoided, because there's no awareness."

rows.jp: 「猫が車の前に飛び出すみたいに」
rows.en: “Like a cat darting in front of a car.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "It's like a cat running out in front a car."
ghs.assessment: The source compares it to a cat darting in front of a car. The English omits “of” after “in front.”
ghs.remedy: Use “Like a cat darting out in front of a car.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "It's like a cat running out in front a car."

rows.jp: 「……自制しないといけない。細心の注意でもって」
rows.en: “...I have to keep myself under control. Exercise the utmost caution.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "...having no self-control is unacceptable. You have to be meticulously careful."
ghs.assessment: The source says he must restrain himself with meticulous care. The English condemns lacking self-control in general, then shifts the instruction to “you.”
ghs.remedy: Use “I have to restrain myself—with the utmost care.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "...having no self-control is unacceptable. You have to be meticulously careful."

ghs.en: Taichi: "But,"

rows.jp: 「毎日楽しくて、つい忘れてしまうんだ。自分が何者かってことを」
rows.en: “Every day is so much fun, I let myself forget what I am.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "every day's so fun, so I just up and forget it all. About who or what I am I mean."
Taichi: "I am---"
Nanaka stirred just slightly.

rows.jp: 今度は本当に虚を突かれて、予測する間もなかった。
rows.en: This time, she truly caught me flat-footed. I had no chance to guess what was coming.

ghs.en: This time it really came out of left field, with no time for prediction either.
Taichi: "Eh...?"

rows.jp: 「楽しいって、言えるなら、いいじゃん」
rows.en: “If you can still say you’re having fun, then that’s enough.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "You said it's fun, and if you can say that, 's all good."

rows.jp: あいまいな胸の柔らかさ。
rows.en: The soft, indistinct press of her breasts.

ghs.en: The ambiguous softness of a breast.
The scent of a girl.

rows.jp: 不思議と、猥雑なものは感じない。
rows.en: Strangely, none of it felt lewd.

ghs.en: Inexplicably, I feel nothing out of order.
ghs.assessment: 猥雑 refers to something vulgar, obscene, or sexually sordid. “Out of order” means improper or broken and does not convey that register.
ghs.remedy: Use “Strangely, I felt nothing vulgar or obscene.”

highlights.text: Inexplicably, I feel nothing out of order.

rows.jp: 抱かれた時の感覚が、曜子さんとは違った。
rows.en: Being held by her felt different from being held by Youko.

ghs.en: The feeling at the moment of embrace was so different from Youko-chan's.
ghs.assessment: The source calls her 曜子さん, Youko-san. The English changes the honorific to “-chan,” altering the relationship marker.
ghs.remedy: Use “Youko-san.”

highlights.text: The feeling at the moment of embrace was so different from Youko-chan's.

rows.jp: 「その言葉は、嬉しいんだ。すごく」
rows.en: “I’m so glad to hear you say that. I really am.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Those words... they make me happy. Really."
Taichi: "......"

rows.jp: 「強くならないと生きる資格がないわけじゃないから」
rows.en: “You don’t have to be strong to deserve to live.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Because never becoming strong is not a disqualification from living."
Nanaka: "Remaining weak is... still fine."
Taichi: "But remaining weak, really..."
Understanding.
ghs.assessment: The source states that she knows something. Nominal “Understanding” removes both subject and the active state of knowing.
ghs.remedy: Use “She knows.”

highlights.text: Understanding.

rows.jp: 彼女は何かを知っている？

ghs.en: What does she understand?
ghs.assessment: The source wonders whether she knows something, not what particular proposition she understands. The English presupposes understanding and asks for its object.
ghs.remedy: Use “Does she know something?”

highlights.text: What does she understand?

ghs.en: Taichi: "You are---"
Nanaka: "Nanaka."
Taichi: "Nanaka..."
No understanding.
ghs.assessment: The source states “I don’t know,” referring to her identity or name. “No understanding” is an impersonal nominal fragment.
ghs.remedy: Use “I don’t know her.”

highlights.text: No understanding.

rows.jp: 過去のいかなる軸にも、その名前は記録されていない。
rows.en: Nowhere along any axis of my past was that name recorded.

ghs.en: On absolutely no axis of the past is that name recorded.

rows.jp: じゃあどうして彼女は俺のことを？
rows.en: Then how did she know me?

ghs.en: Well then why does she... me...?
ghs.assessment: The source asks how she knows about him. “Why does she... me...?” omits the governing verb and never forms the relation.
ghs.remedy: Use “Then how does she know about me?”

highlights.text: Well then why does she... me...?

ghs.en: Nanaka: "You calmed down?"
Taichi: "...yeah."
We distance from each other.
ghs.assessment: 身を離す omits its subject and can be realized reciprocally as the embrace ends. The defects are present tense and unidiomatic distance from each other.
ghs.remedy: Use We drew apart.

highlights.text: We distance from each other.

rows.jp: 七香はにこにこと笑っている。

ghs.en: Nanaka is smiling broad and bright.
Taichi: "...say, you."
Taichi: "Are you in love with me or something?"
Nanaka: "Ya dum'ass!"

rows.en: She chopped me on the forehead.

ghs.en: Chopped right on the forehead.
Nanaka: "Told ya that ain't it!"

rows.jp: 否定してから、小首を傾げて言葉の穂を継いだ。
rows.en: After denying it, she cocked her head and went on.

ghs.en: After the denial, she tilted her head in doubt and continued on the ear of the words she had left.
ghs.assessment: The source idiom means she tilts her head and continues speaking. “Continued on the ear of the words she had left” literalizes components into nonsense.
ghs.remedy: Use “After denying it, she tilted her head slightly and continued.”

highlights.text: After the denial, she tilted her head in doubt and continued on the ear of the words she had left.

rows.en: “...But maybe I do. Maybe I like you.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "...but, riiight. I might just love you!"
Taichi: "Really?"

rows.jp: 「あんたの思う好きとは、ちょっと意味が違うけどね」
rows.en: “Just not the kind of like you’re thinking of.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "But it's got a sorta different meaning from the kind of love yer thinking of."
Taichi: "Dun' getcha..."

rows.jp: 「あんたってさ、きっと子供の頃、母親にＨな悪戯するタイプだよ」
rows.en: “You strike me as the kind of kid who would’ve gotten handsy with his mother.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Ya know you, I'm sure that you were the type to play perverted sexual pranks on your mother when you were a kid."
Taichi: "Thassnottrue!"
ghs.assessment: Taichi’s retort says he did not have a mother. “That’s not true” merely denies her personality claim and removes the biographical fact.
ghs.remedy: Use “I didn’t have one.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Thassnottrue!"

ghs.en: Nanaka: "I was the same."

rows.jp: 「でもさ、そーいうのって、けっこう母親も嬉しいのかもよ？」
rows.en: “Still, maybe mothers actually enjoy that sort of thing?”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "But yannow, all that said, surely mother's gonna be happy too, right?"
ghs.assessment: The source suggests mothers may actually be rather pleased by such behavior. “Mother’s gonna be happy too” makes one mother future-certain and leaves “too” without a comparison.
ghs.remedy: Use “But maybe mothers are actually pretty happy about that kind of thing.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "But yannow, all that said, surely mother's gonna be happy too, right?"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Of perverted sexual pranks?"
ghs.assessment: Taichi incredulously asks whether the sexual prank itself would please a mother. “Of perverted sexual pranks?” is not a grammatical echo question.
ghs.remedy: Use “The naughty prank would make her happy?”

highlights.text: Taichi: "Of perverted sexual pranks?"

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Yep."

rows.jp: 「でも幼い息子にペッティングされたらショック……いや、むしろ萌えか？」
rows.en: “But if your little boy started feeling you up, wouldn’t that be horrifying? ...Or maybe it’d turn you on?”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But heavy petting from a young offspring's a bit shocking... nah, should I say maybe moe?"

rows.jp: 「化学分解されてしまえこの有害ゴミめが」
rows.en: “Go break down into your constituent chemicals, you piece of hazardous garbage.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Go chemically decompose, you damn toxic garbage!"
Taichi: "Bwaaah!"
Nanaka: "So then, I should go home."

rows.jp: 「うちに寄ってけばいいのに。ぬるい水くらい出すぞ」
rows.en: “You could stop by my place. I can offer you some lukewarm water.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "But you can come inside no problem. I can at least bring out the lukewarmish water!"

rows.jp: 「ニヒヒ、Ｈなことされたくないから帰る」
rows.en: “Nyehehe. I’m going home before you can try anything dirty.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Nihihih, I don't wanna have perverted stuff done to me so going h-o-m-e."

rows.en: “Oh, I would. Come over and find out.”

ghs.en: Taichi: "I will, I will, come in and I will!"
ghs.assessment: The source says he would do it if she came in. “Come in and I will” turns the condition into an imperative addressed to her.
ghs.remedy: Use “I would, I would. If you came in, I’d do it.”

highlights.text: Taichi: "I will, I will, come in and I will!"

ghs.en: Nanaka: "Too dangerous, too dangerous!"

rows.jp: 彼女はさっそうと自転車にまたがる。
rows.en: With a flourish, she swung onto her bicycle.

ghs.en: She jauntily sits astride the bicycle.

rows.jp: 背後にまわって下着を見ようとする俺。
rows.en: I circled around behind her for a look at her underwear.

ghs.en: And turning to my back and attempting to see her underwear go I.
ghs.assessment: The source says he moves around behind her to look at her underwear. “Turning to my back” reverses the direction, and “go I” is malformed inversion.
ghs.remedy: Use “I circled around behind her to look at her underwear.”

highlights.text: And turning to my back and attempting to see her underwear go I.

rows.jp: ノーコンのブルマだった。

ghs.en:
Buruma Out of Control*.
* Dark blue
ghs.assessment: The source identifies the bloomers’ dark navy color. “Out of Control” invents a meaning for ノーコン, while the footnote only partially repairs the mistranslation.
ghs.remedy: Use “They were dark navy bloomers.”

highlights.text:
Buruma Out of Control*.
* Dark blue

ghs.en: Taichi: "Tsk!"
...wait, they're buruma?!

rows.jp: 女性解放運動も真っ青なセクハラ体操着としてずいぶん前に絶滅したという、ブルマ！？
rows.en: Bloomers?! That notorious piece of sexual-harassment gymwear, supposedly extinct for years—enough to make the women’s liberation movement blanch?!

ghs.en: That deep blue gym sexual harassment-ish uniform hunted down to extinction a fair while ago by the women's lib movement, that is, buruma?!
ghs.assessment: The source says the bloomers were so harassing that even the women’s liberation movement would pale, and that they went extinct long ago. The English makes that movement the agent that hunted them down.
ghs.remedy: Use “Bloomers—the harassing gymwear, enough to make even the women’s liberation movement blanch, said to have gone extinct long ago!?”

highlights.text: That deep blue gym sexual harassment-ish uniform hunted down to extinction a fair while ago by the women's lib movement, that is, buruma?!

ghs.en: Taichi: "Na-, Nanaka-san...?"

rows.jp: 俺はわなわなと震えた。

ghs.en: I shook and trembled with fear.
ghs.assessment: The source says he trembles violently; it does not specify fear. The surrounding reaction may instead be shock or excitement.
ghs.remedy: Use “I trembled violently.”

highlights.text: I shook and trembled with fear.

rows.jp: 噂によれば、そのヒップへの張りつき具合は絶品だと言う。
rows.en: Rumor had it, nothing hugged an ass quite like them.

ghs.en: Rumors have it that what is clinging firmly to those hips is a superlative article.
ghs.assessment: The rumor praises how exquisitely the bloomers cling to the hips. The English calls the object itself “a superlative article” and loses the quality of the fit.
ghs.remedy: Use “Rumor says the way they cling to the hips is exquisite.”

highlights.text: Rumors have it that what is clinging firmly to those hips is a superlative article.

rows.jp: 「アンテナ、ちゃっちゃっと組み立てちゃいなさいよね」
rows.en: “Get that antenna put together, and make it snappy.”

ghs.en: Nanaka: "And that antenna, you go put it up pretty and fast!"
ghs.assessment: The source tells him to assemble the antenna briskly. “Pretty and fast” treats ちゃっちゃっと as two separate qualities.
ghs.remedy: Use “Put that antenna together, and make it quick.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "And that antenna, you go put it up pretty and fast!"

ghs.en: Taichi: "Ah, the antenna?"
All of a sudden.
Nanaka: "That is... possibilities, 's what."
ghs.assessment: The source identifies the antenna as a possibility in the singular conceptual sense. “That is possibilities” has number disagreement and changes the abstraction.
ghs.remedy: Use “Because that antenna represents possibility.”

highlights.text: Nanaka: "That is... possibilities, 's what."

rows.jp: チェーンが小気味よい音をたてて、まわる。
rows.en: The chain ran with a crisp, cheerful rattle.

ghs.en: The chain spin, making a most delightful sound.
ghs.assessment: The singular subject “chain” requires “spins.”
ghs.remedy: Use “The chain spins with a crisp, pleasant sound.”

highlights.text: The chain spin, making a most delightful sound.

rows.jp: タイヤがアスファルトを擦り、自転車が走り出す。
rows.en: The tires rasped over the asphalt, and the bicycle sped away.

ghs.en: The tire graze the asphalt as the bicycle begins to ride forth.
ghs.assessment: The singular “tire” requires “grazes,” and a bicycle itself begins to move or roll rather than “ride forth.”
ghs.remedy: Use “The tire grazes the asphalt, and the bicycle rolls away.”

highlights.text: The tire graze the asphalt as the bicycle begins to ride forth.

ghs.en: Taichi: "...what was with that."
